plain_english_title: Key Date Cutoffs: Informal Claims (2015), Severance Offsets (1996/2008), Pension Transfers (2018) & Debt Waivers (2022/2026)
what_this_means: Across VA compensation, wartime pension, and overpayment law, a handful of sharp calendar cutoffs determine whether an older medical visit counts as a claim, how much separation pay VA can recoup, whether gifting assets triggers a pension penalty, and how long you have to request a debt waiver. This historical comparison maps four major rule shifts side-by-side: (1) March 24, 2015 (when Intent to File replaced informal claims and VA hospital-report claims under former 38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b)), (2) October 1, 1996 and January 28, 2008 (after-tax separation/severance recoupment caps and combat-zone severance exemptions under 38 C.F.R. § 3.700), (3) October 18, 2018 (bright-line pension net worth and 36-month transfer lookback under 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.274–3.279), and (4) December 29, 2022 / January 26, 2026 (expansion of the overpayment waiver window from 180 days to 1 year under 38 U.S.C. § 5302(a) and 38 C.F.R. § 1.963(b)).
record_clues: A pre-March 24, 2015 VA medical center outpatient exam or hospital admission showing worsening of an already service-connected disability (including a 0% rating) that VA never adjudicated as an informal claim for increase under former 38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b).

A VA Award Letter recouping gross pre-tax separation or severance pay received after September 30, 1996, OR recouping Chapter 61 combat-zone / combat-related disability severance pay for a separation on or after January 28, 2008.
A VA Pension denial applying a 36-month transfer penalty to a gift or trust created before October 18, 2018, or where total net worth was already below VA's bright-line limit.

A Debt Management Center or Committee on Waivers and Compromises letter dismissing a waiver request filed 181–365 days after a post-December 29, 2022 debt notice based on the outdated 180-day regulation.
important_cautions: Prospective military separation cutoffs: the combat-zone / combat-related disability severance non-recoupment rule (10 U.S.C. § 1212(d)(2)) applies strictly to service members separated on or after January 28, 2008, and the after-tax net recoupment cap applies strictly to separation/severance payments made after September 30, 1996.

March 24, 2015 claim-form cutoff: VA medical records generated ON OR AFTER March 24, 2015 do NOT automatically initiate a claim for increase—though pre-March 24, 2015 informal claims that VA never adjudicated remain viable (Shea v. Wilkie).

October 18, 2018 pension transfer cutoff: pre-October 18, 2018 asset transfers are exempt from the 36-month penalty period, whereas uncompensated transfers of excess assets ON OR AFTER October 18, 2018 can trigger up to a 5-year pension penalty.

Judicial invalidation vs. CUE: while the Federal Circuit invalidated VA's ban on Intent to File for Supplemental Claims in Military-Veterans Advocacy v. Secretary of Veterans Affairs (July 30, 2021), George v. McDonough and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e) bar using that later court ruling to claim Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) against final pre-July 30, 2021 decisions.
questions_for_representative: Do my pre-March 24, 2015 VA medical center records contain an unadjudicated informal claim for increase under former 38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b)?

Did VA calculate my separation or disability severance recoupment using my net after-tax payout (post-September 30, 1996), or exempt my Chapter 61 combat-related severance pay if I separated on or after January 28, 2008?
If VA denied my Wartime or Survivors Pension due to an asset transfer, did the transfer happen before October 18, 2018 or stay below the bright-line net-worth threshold?
Was my overpayment waiver filed within 1 year of a debt notice dated on or after December 29, 2022 under 38 U.S.C. § 5302(a)?
